glance: 27 km to Gazipur by road, 1–2 hours by bus or car
isa-khan-tomb-bakhtarpur.desc: Isa Khan led the Baro Bhuiyans, the Bengal chiefs who resisted the Mughals in the late 16th century. After he died in September 1599 he was buried at Bakhtarpur in what is now Kaliganj upazila of Gazipur. For a long time the exact spot was uncertain, but research on the site and its old remains settled on Bakhtarpur. In December 2021 a new memorial structure was built and opened over the grave. It is a quiet village stop for anyone following Isa Khan's story from Sonargaon to Kishoreganj.
blocks: How to get there
From Gazipur or Tongi take a bus or CNG to Kaliganj, then a CNG or easy-bike to Bakhtarpur village.
Good to know
It is a village site with few facilities; ask locals for 'Isa Khan-er kobor'. Pair it with Isa Khan's sites at Sonargaon or Egarosindur if you are tracing the Baro Bhuiyans.

glance: Sold per hundred; price varies with variety and size
Orchard roads and bazaars of Kapasia and Sreepur
gazipur-lychee.desc: Alongside jackfruit, Kapasia and Sreepur grow plenty of lychee, harvested over a few weeks in May and June. Growers cut whole branches and tie the fruit into bunches of a hundred, which is how they are counted and sold. Freshly picked fruit has thin, red skin and very juicy flesh. The season is short, so if you are in Gazipur then, look for orchard-side sellers.

glance: Approx. 100–400 BDT per fruit depending on size
Roadside stalls and haats in Kapasia and Sreepur
gazipur-jackfruit.desc: The raised red-soil land of Gazipur suits jackfruit trees, and Kapasia and Sreepur are among the country's best-known growing areas. In early summer the trees are heavy with fruit hanging straight off the trunk, and roadside stalls pile them up along the highways. The ripe pods are honey-sweet and fragrant; the seeds are boiled or added to curries, and young green jackfruit is cooked like a vegetable. Buying one straight from a grower is a classic Gazipur experience.

glance: 27 km to Gazipur by road, 1–2 hours by bus or car
nagari-church.desc: Portuguese missionaries settled in the Bhawal area in the 16th–17th centuries and founded this church at Nagari in 1664, with Mughal permission; a brick building followed in 1680 and the present old church dates from an 1888 rebuild. Its single-storey hall mixes European and local styles, with a verandah of three arched entrances. Beside it stand a newer church built in 2009, two old cemeteries and a school. While posted here, the priest Manoel da Assumpção wrote the first grammar and dictionary of the Bengali language.
blocks: How to get there
From Gazipur or Tongi take a bus or CNG to Kaliganj, then an auto or CNG to Nagari.
Good to know
It is an active parish, so visit outside Mass times and ask before photographing inside. Christmas brings a big local gathering.

glance: 27 km to Gazipur by road, 1–2 hours by bus or car
nuhash-polli.desc: Humayun Ahmed, the country's most loved novelist and filmmaker, built this rural estate at Pirujali and used it as a shooting location and writing retreat. The grounds have a pond with a wooden ghat, a small medicinal-plant garden, sculptures and hundreds of fruit and flowering trees. He was buried here in 2012, and fans still come to pay respects. It is calm and green, a gentle contrast to Gazipur's industrial roads.
blocks: How to get there
From Gazipur Chowrasta take a CNG towards Pirujali; ask for Nuhash Polli.
Good to know
Opening days and rules change; check before going.

baliadi-zamindar-bari.desc: The Baliadi estate was founded by a family that traced its line to Mughal-era officers granted land in the Talebabad pargana in the early 17th century. Later generations moved to Baliadi village in Kaliakair and built the zamindar house that stands there today. The family produced several well-known public figures in the 20th century. The house is off the usual tourist route and makes a quiet stop on a Kaliakair or Safari Park day.
blocks: How to get there
From Chandra or Kaliakair take a CNG or auto to Baliadi village.
Good to know
Parts of the house may still be in private family use, so ask before going inside.

bishwa-ijtema-tongi.desc: Every winter, usually in January, the Tablighi Jamaat hosts the Bishwa Ijtema on a large open ground beside the Turag river at Tongi. Over two sessions, vast numbers of people from Bangladesh and abroad camp under canvas for days of prayer and sermons. The closing prayer, the Akheri Munajat, draws crowds that spill onto highways and rooftops. It is a religious event rather than a tourist one, but seeing the scale of it is unforgettable.
blocks: Good to know
Expect heavy traffic and road closures around Tongi; non-participants should keep a respectful distance.

bhawal-national-park.desc: Bhawal National Park protects a remnant of the sal forest that once covered much of this part of central Bangladesh. Tall, straight sal trees shade dirt paths, small lakes and picnic areas with named cottages. Weekends and winter holidays bring crowds of picnickers, but on weekday mornings it is quiet enough to hear woodpeckers and spot monkeys. The forest is at its greenest after the first monsoon rains.
blocks: How to get there
Bus along the Dhaka–Mymensingh highway to the park gate near Rajendrapur, about 1–1.5 hours from Dhaka.
Good to know
Visit on a weekday morning; avoid winter weekends when picnic groups bring loudspeakers.

glance: 27 km to Gazipur by road, 1–2 hours by bus or car
bhawal-rajbari.desc: The Bhawal Raj estate controlled much of Gazipur's forest land, and its palace at Joydebpur is a long, two-storey building with a deep verandah and courtyards. It is best remembered for the Bhawal Sannyasi case, in which a holy man claimed in the 1920s to be the second prince, believed dead years earlier, and won in court. The building now houses government offices, so access inside is limited. The exterior and grounds are worth a short stop for anyone interested in the story.
blocks: How to get there
In Joydebpur, Gazipur city; reachable by rickshaw from Joydebpur railway station.
Good to know
It is an office building; ask the guard before entering the grounds and visit during working hours.

bhawal-raj-shmashaneshwari.desc: About a kilometre north of the Bhawal Rajbari, on the south bank of the Chilai river, lies the place where the Bhawal zamindars cremated their dead. The complex has seven memorial maths, a Shiva temple and tomb-like monuments with name plaques, built of lime, brick-dust mortar and terracotta. Locally it is also called the Raj-Rajeshwari temple, and Kali, Saraswati and Shiva pujas are still held here. It was declared a protected monument in 2017, yet few visitors to Gazipur know it exists.
blocks: How to get there
From Joydebpur or the Bhawal Rajbari (DC office) take a rickshaw or auto north to Uttar Chhayabithi.
Good to know
Pair it with the Bhawal Rajbari, which is close by. It is a religious site, so be respectful during puja.

glance: Separate tickets for entry and safari bus (approx.)
gazipur-safari-park.desc: The safari park near Sreepur covers a large area of sal forest, divided into a core safari zone and a walk-around section. Visitors ride closed buses through enclosures holding Bengal tigers, lions, bears, deer and zebras. Outside the drive there are aviaries, a butterfly area and a nature museum. It is a popular family day trip from Dhaka and Gazipur.
blocks: How to get there
Bus on the Dhaka–Mymensingh highway to Baghher Bazar, then a short CNG ride to the gate.
Good to know
Usually closed one weekday each week; check before going. Arrive early to avoid long safari queues.
